content.thinking:
Setting up imports for the file, pulling in Three.js along with the builder, frame, and part option types I'll need for this module.

I'm defining a small palette system with wood grain textures across different axes, lacquer colors, and a planked wood paint helper for the tabletop surface.

Writing wood paint logic...

Now I'm moving on to writing SVG strings for textures like the rug pattern.

Generating diamond border patterns...

Then I'm planning simpler assets: a table runner with teal border and gold dots, and a wall chart texture showing a parchment elemental circle with glyphs, scribbled text, and tattered edges with wooden rods—plus a transmutation circle design.

Now I'm sketching the drawer plate: a dark teal rounded rect with gold filigree swirls and a central diamond, using mirrored curling paths for the ornate scrollwork.

I'm then planning the door filigree panel with gold corners and a petaled flower center, followed by book cover variants with gold frames, corner ornaments, and gem emblems, plus spine designs with gold bands and title text, and finally the page layouts.

For pages I'm defining left and right page textures with a diagram and text with an initial letter, then moving to labels, and figuring out the tassel design -- noting that since the card hangs with a 180-degree lean, I need to draw the knot at the bottom of the SVG and fringe at top so it reads correctly once flipped, same logic applying to the herb stem placement.

Now I'm sketching out the botanical and decorative assets: a broad leaf with stem at bottom, a fern, lavender buds, a glazed lily with petals glowing at top, a hanging dried herb sprig, a gold sparkle star, a smaller reused rune circle, and a cream-teal quill feather as a double-sided card -- and I'm pausing on whether to bother texturing the lantern or just build it geometrically.

I'm tallying up all the texture assets needed -- rugs, runners, charts, book covers, spines, pages, labels, plants, sparkle, feather -- roughly 35 pieces each with tinted variants, and checking whether a 4096 atlas can fit everything alongside the paint sheet, possibly needing to shrink the paint size back down.

Now I'm defining the potion system's types and element data, setting up a function signature for placing potions with color, glyph, and shape variants, and starting to build out the elements table.

I'm sketching the geometric profiles for each potion shape -- round bottles with curved bodies and narrow necks, tall thin vials, flat box-like flasks, and gourd shapes made from two stacked spheres -- defining the radius-and-height coordinate pairs that will be lathed or extruded into 3D liquid and glass forms.

I'm also planning the finishing details: faceted hexagonal variants, glass necks with flared bases, gold rings at the neck, cork stoppers, wax seals, and small highlight capsules positioned on the upper body to simulate light reflection.

I'm applying glow to the capsule part, then setting up a decal for the liquid label positioned on the front surface with appropriate size and segments, adjusting for flat box shapes where the surface sits at a slightly different depth.

For bottle decoration, I'm working out how to add a tassel at the neck ring positioned slightly forward, with hanging cards collected into an array and drawn together so they read correctly from the front, accounting for how the shape hangs along the vertical axis below the neck.

I'm realizing the tassel would intersect the body's shoulder curve if placed too close, since the shoulder narrows but still has enough radius to collide with a hanging cord starting near the neck base -- so I need to push the frame forward enough (around 5cm) to clear the shoulder while still looking attached via a floating cord.

Rather than fighting bottle tassels, I'll simplify by skipping them there and instead using a wax seal with ribbon wrap on the cork plus a hanging label tag. Tassels and ribbons will instead go on better-suited spots: hutch roof corners, the lantern, drawer pulls, bookmarks hanging out of books, scale chain bottoms, and the lamp, with large jars getting hang tags instead. I also need to work out the pan's chain position and plan for potions sitting in floor crates.

For the herb jars, I'm deciding on a lathe-built glass jar with an opaque painted body matching its contents -- mottled green for dried herbs, spotted red for berries, purple for dried flowers -- with a pale glass neck and cork lid, possibly showing a mound of contents above the rim, or alternatively going with painted Liyue-style porcelain apothecary jars with lids and labels.

Ceramic jars will be the main approach: lathe-built forms painted cream porcelain with teal band stripes, a domed knobbed lid, and a label decal, plus a few glass jars showing visible pearl-sphere contents.

Now I'm defining the embedding depth for items on the shelf -- setting the top surface and runner plane heights so pieces sit flush with a slight 1.5mm recess into the surface.

Now I'm building the scale pillar itself: a tapered cylinder stem with torus collar rings rotated flat, a sphere finial on top, and a pivoting sphere at the beam's center. For the beam, I'm using tapered rod geometry with small knob spheres and hanging torus rings at each end to hold the chains for the pans.

Adding the gold indicator needle...

Still shaping the pan profile and positioning the hanging chain points around the rim...

I'm filling the pan with contents - a stack of gold coin cylinders on one side and a cluster of leaves, berries, and a cross-like shape on the other, setting their relative positions above the pan floor. Now I'm thinking about adding a wall-mounted lantern bracket extending outward from the right support post.

I'm positioning the lantern on an angled arm reaching diagonally from the post toward the eave, with the lantern body hanging below on a short chain near the roofline, and considering adding a hanging hook with tools like a ladle or funnel on the left post to balance the composition.

Rather than more small hanging props, I'll move on to committing the full code now, starting with the roof geometry — defining its outline in the side profile and working out the thickness direction using the cross product of the relevant axes.

Still writing shape coordinates...

Working through the concave sag at each point along the profile, I'm settling on a sequence of coordinates for the top and underside curves, including a sharp tip near (0.37, 0.055) and a sharp ridge near (-0.13, 0.2), to define the full outline.

For the roof body, I'm planning a depth of 2.2, with the bottom resting at y=1.92 and the posts tucked under the front edge. I also want to add a darker wooden ceiling detail underneath and a row of small cylindrical rafter-ends along the front eave to suggest exposed beams.

Now I'm adding gold caps on those rafter ends as a row of merged cylinders, plus a dark fascia board at the front edge and a red lacquer lintel beam attached to the roof's underside near the front, since there's no front post to support it otherwise.

I'm also sketching the ridge cap with gold rod and finial spheres/cones at the ends, figuring the overall height comes to about 2.17, and now I'm tallying up the total model width bounds.

The prop cluster ends up roughly 3 units wide by 1 deep by 2.17 tall, which feels reasonable for a dressing cluster—I'll adjust the cauldron position slightly inward and move on to writing concrete code for each prop using helper functions for shapes like torus rings and gold bands on cylinders.

I'm now building a book-flat function that lays a closed book down with spine facing the viewer, handling rotation by computing local offsets around the book's center.

Each book is assembled from a top and bottom board, a thin spine plate, an inset page block, and small gold corner caps for decoration.

Still placing decal orientation details, then moving to standing-shelf books: a function that boxes the cover, decals the spine texture facing the viewer, and adds visible page edges on top.

Writing leaf placement logic...

For the cards I'll skip bend and instead add a slight lean for tipping toward the flow direction. Then I'm sketching out the painted stripe pattern for the wicker basket texture and working out the lathe profile points for the barrel's bulging silhouette.

Finishing the barrel shape, I'm adding the metal hoops as thin torus rings positioned at points where the radius bulges, colored like dark iron, plus a lid disc capping the top.

For the sacks, I'm defining a lathe profile that bulges and tapers to a tied neck with a rope ring and painted mottled cloth texture, with herb leaves poking out the top. For crates, I'm sketching plank-textured boxes with corner posts and slat frames.

Now I'm working out the crate construction: a body box painted with horizontal seam stripes to mimic planking, darker corner posts, and gold studs, plus bottles poking out the top with a flat straw-textured box standing in for tufted straw.

For the under-bench shelf I'm placing a teal lathed amphora with a gold band, a basket of herbs, a smaller crate of bottles, and a stack of books. On the bench itself I'm adding a copper funnel, wall-hung tongs, an hourglass built from two cones and a frame, and a glowing crystal cluster on a stand, aiming to keep the whole scene tidy despite the growing part count — roughly 500 parts total — while locking in the tabletop layout coordinates, starting with the lectern and open book position.

Now I'm working through placement of the remaining tabletop items, checking for overlaps between the book stack, candle, inkwell, scales, weight tray, and mortar, then laying out a back row of porcelain jars under the shelf while making sure they clear the scales' base and pans.

I'm positioning the alembic burner and receiving bottle near the scale pan, adding flat leaves by the mortar, and arranging a right-front row of potion bottles along with a mushroom basket and potted plant, double-checking each against the weights tray for clearance.

Now I'm placing a lavender vase near the left lectern, then shifting to the mid shelf layout where I'm spacing out seven potions evenly across the shelf width.

For the upper shelf I'm planning books on the left, a crystal centered, jars to the right, with enough clearance below the roof for anything under 0.3 tall. I also need to check that hanging herbs near the rail don't collide with the taller shelf items.

Now I'm positioning the herb bundles along the rail with spacing on each side, and figuring out how to support the rail itself using small rods hanging from the lintel.

I'll offset each herb bundle with a few frames so cards cross-grow into bushy clusters, with cards leaning 180 so they hang downward. For tassels, I'm adding frames at the roof's front corners hanging long and thin, and considering whether to add gold bells too.

I'm defining a color palette next—whites, flame oranges and yellows, glowing greens and teals, lantern and ink-dark tones—then moving into writing the actual scene code, being careful with rotation parameters in degrees. For the crystal cluster I'll use stretched octahedron geometries grouped in fives with a cryo glow color.

Writing scene code...

Working out the page tilt angles so each half's outer edge lifts slightly, then figuring how to compose that with the lectern's own 22° tilt around the x-axis without the rotations conflicting.

I'll build a small helper that combines a group's origin and rotation into a quaternion, letting me transform local offsets into the tilted frame — reusable for the lectern, books, and similar rotated parts. Writing the group frame helper...

I note lathe doesn't support quat, so rotated groups only work with boxes, cylinders, planes, and spheres via part, and rotated books only with boxes. For decal planes I'll add a `dir` helper that applies the group's quaternion to a direction vector, confirming orientation priority goes to quat when both quat and at are given. Now I'm ready to write the full implementation.

Writing SVG card label generators...

Writing glyph markup...

Now I'm sketching out the potion generator function, defining shape variants and positioning logic for the liquid, neck, and label elements, starting with the round shape case.

Now I'm planning the rest of the bottle: a gold decorative foot ring, a glass neck with its own gold torus accent, a frustum-shaped cork topped with a colored wax seal, and finishing touches like a white highlight capsule and small label decal for realism.

I'll skip visible bubbles for now and instead use sparkle cards near the alembic, scale, lectern, and cauldron for ambient magical effect, importing the frame helper and placing small gold/teal sparkle textures randomly around those props.

I need to verify that glow() correctly handles arrays of meshes as its target, since I'm calling it on groups of cards.

input.command: sed -n 1,80p kits/glow.ts; grep -n "cards(" src/builder.ts; grep -n "export type CardOptions" -A40 src/cards.ts | head -70
